title: Bearings and Support Details
case_name: C016 - Bearings and Support Details (journal values, feb1bb316d08)
intro: **What it does.** The bearing and support details of the pedestrian bridge: the end-bent cap dimension chain of SDM Fig. 12.5-1, the minimum support length N of LRFD 4.7.4.4 at the pier pedestal, the Type F bearing-pad service-gravity screening of each pier bearing, the level pier bearing-seat rotation and movement screen against the SPI 400-510 limits using the saved beam-worksheet rotations, and the adopted level as-cast seat elevations.
overview: Support details at the pier and end bents. The cap width chain assembles the cover, bar inset, pad length and beam-end dimensions of SDM Fig. 12.5-1. The empirical minimum support length of LRFD Eq. 4.7.4.4-1 is compared with the support length the full-length pier pedestal provides.

Each pier bearing is screened against the standard Type F pad service limits for the adopted skew; the level pier seats are screened for static and cyclic rotation from the profile grade and the saved camber and dead-load rotations of the span worksheets, for the cyclic direction, and for longitudinal thermal plus creep movement against the pad shear-deflection limit. The adopted level as-cast seat elevations at all three supports are recorded.
outside: the final bearing setting and grinding, the pad design itself and the superstructure camber analysis.

BearingPad_length: This is dimension C in the embedded Figure 12.5-1. Measure the pad in the direction of the illustrated cap-width calculation. It occupies the part of the chain where the beam bears on the pad.
Cap_cover: This is dimension A in the embedded cap-width figure. It reserves concrete between the exposed cap edge and the reinforcement. The separate B dimension then moves the bearing pad farther inside the reinforcement.
Fig_12_5_1_DimB: This is dimension B in the embedded Figure 12.5-1. It moves the pad inward beyond the steel location, after the concrete cover has already been counted. It is not additional pad length.
Fig_12_5_1_DimD: This is dimension D in the embedded Figure 12.5-1. The entered value follows the figure’s no-diaphragm option. This distance is added after the bearing-pad length to reserve the shown space near the beam end.
Fig_12_5_1_DimF: The displayed expression divides the 3 in separation by 2. It therefore contributes half that separation to this one-sided calculation. In the embedded double-bearing figure, F labels the separation between the opposing end details; the journal uses a half-share here for the stated end-bent adaptation.
Cap_width_min: The result is the sum of this one-sided chain for the end-bent adaptation noted above. The displayed expression does not double the chain or include the diaphragm-extension dimension E from the embedded double-bearing figure; it should not be read as that figure’s full two-bearing formula.

working_notes: The calculation was ported from the journal module BearingDesign (journal feb1bb316d08); every definition of the module was evaluated independently from the journal file and reproduced by the notebook to 1 part in 10⁹ before this edition was written.
